P1 Shopping malls
Task: Nowadays young people like spending much of their free time in shopping malls. Do the advantages of this development outweigh its disadvantages?
Suggested complete response | 284 words

Shopping malls have become popular places for young people to spend their free time. They provide convenient spaces for meeting friends and enjoying entertainment. However, I believe the disadvantages outweigh these benefits when shopping becomes a dominant leisure activity, particularly because of the pressure on personal budgets and time.

There are understandable reasons for enjoying a visit to a mall. Several facilities are available in one place, so friends can meet for a meal, see a film or browse shops without arranging separate journeys. Indoor spaces may also be convenient when the weather makes outdoor activities uncomfortable. Some young shoppers can practise making sensible decisions by comparing prices and following a fixed budget. These experiences show that a mall visit does not have to involve excessive spending. Used occasionally, it can be a useful part of a varied social routine.

The difficulties arise when frequent visits encourage people to purchase things they do not need. Promotions and displays can make a small purchase seem harmless, yet repeated spending can consume a substantial part of a limited budget. A student who regularly buys new clothes may have less money for transport or educational materials. There is also an opportunity cost: time spent shopping can replace exercise, creative projects or inexpensive community activities. These alternatives develop skills and relationships without requiring continual purchases. Since the financial and time costs can recur every week, they may be more significant than the temporary pleasure of buying another product.

In conclusion, shopping malls offer convenient entertainment and social opportunities, but these benefits do not justify allowing shopping to dominate young people’s leisure time. The disadvantages are greater when repeated visits create unnecessary spending and crowd out more varied activities.
Check the answer

Outweigh essay. Possible view: The disadvantages are greater when shopping takes up too much leisure time. Limit: Do not assume every mall visit involves buying goods. Vocabulary: impulse purchases; consumer spending; leisure activities.
P2 Threats to animal species
Task: Animal species are becoming extinct due to human activities on land and in the sea. What are the reasons and solutions?
Suggested complete response | 291 words

Human activities are placing many animal species under pressure on land and in the sea. Habitat destruction and excessive exploitation are two important causes. Protecting living environments and controlling the use of wildlife resources are therefore necessary responses, particularly when these measures are backed by effective monitoring.

On land, clearing forests for development or production can remove the places where animals feed and reproduce. A species may struggle even if some forest remains, because isolated areas can make it harder to find food or suitable breeding partners. In marine environments, intensive fishing can reduce populations faster than they recover. When large numbers of animals are removed repeatedly, future reproduction may also decline. These pressures are different from a single temporary disturbance: they can persist over time and affect the conditions needed for a population to survive. Pollution can further damage habitats, adding to the difficulty of recovery.

The solutions need to address these causes directly. Public authorities can protect important habitats from damaging development and restore connections between remaining areas. For example, preserving a breeding site is more useful than declaring an unrelated area protected simply because it is available. Fishing authorities can also set limits appropriate to local conditions and check that those limits are followed. Monitoring catches and enforcing restrictions give the rules practical effect. Communities and businesses that depend on these resources should be involved, because conservation is more sustainable when people understand the rules and have workable alternatives to harmful practices.

In conclusion, species decline is often connected to the loss of suitable habitats and the removal of animals at unsustainable rates. Protection, restoration and properly enforced limits can reduce these pressures. Announcing conservation goals alone is insufficient without the resources and cooperation needed to implement them.
Check the answer
Causes and solutions. Match each response to a source of harm. Limit: A protected area needs management, not just a name. Vocabulary: habitat loss; overexploitation; conservation (bảo tồn).
P3 Antisocial behaviour
Task: These days, there has been an increase in antisocial behaviour and a lack of respect for people. What are the causes and what solutions can be taken?
Suggested complete response | 282 words

Antisocial behaviour and disrespect can make everyday life more difficult for the people affected. Inconsistent guidance about acceptable conduct and weak responses to harmful behaviour may contribute to these problems. Education in respectful interaction, combined with fair enforcement, can help address the causes rather than merely condemn the results.

One possible cause is that some children receive little consistent guidance about managing disagreement. If aggressive behaviour is ignored or modelled by adults, young people may not learn more constructive ways to express frustration. Schools cannot fully compensate when expectations at home are unclear. Another factor is the response to misconduct in public settings. When harassment or intimidation is repeatedly overlooked, those responsible may believe there are few consequences. People affected may also stop reporting incidents if they expect no useful response. This does not mean that every instance has the same cause, but it helps explain how harmful patterns can continue.

Parents and schools can respond by teaching and demonstrating practical alternatives. Children need opportunities to practise listening, resolving conflicts and recognising how their actions affect others. Clear expectations should be applied consistently, while mistakes can become opportunities for learning. Authorities and organisations also need accessible reporting procedures and proportionate consequences for serious misconduct. For example, a transport provider could make it easier to report harassment and ensure that complaints receive a timely response. These measures support people affected and show that rules are meaningful, without treating every disagreement as a criminal matter.

In conclusion, inadequate guidance and ineffective responses can contribute to disrespectful behaviour. Teaching constructive interaction and enforcing clear standards are complementary solutions. Their value depends on consistent practice by families, institutions and the authorities responsible for protecting the public.
Check the answer

Causes and solutions. Focus on behaviour such as harassment, aggression or public disorder. Limit: Avoid blaming an entire generation or treating quietness as antisocial behaviour. Vocabulary: social norms; parental guidance; law enforcement.
P4 Work life balance
Task: Not many people are able to achieve a balance between work and other aspects of life. What are the problems? What solutions can be suggested?
Suggested complete response | 293 words

Many people struggle to balance employment with family responsibilities, rest and other activities. The resulting problems include weaker personal relationships and limited opportunities to recover from demanding work. Employers and households can help by setting reasonable boundaries and distributing responsibilities more fairly.

One consequence of poor balance is the loss of shared time with family and friends. A worker who is regularly available to colleagues during evenings may be physically at home but unable to participate fully in conversations or activities. Over time, this can weaken the support that close relationships provide. Insufficient rest can also make it harder to concentrate and manage daily demands. The problem may be especially difficult when paid work is combined with an unequal share of domestic tasks. A person responsible for most childcare or housework may have fewer opportunities to develop professionally or simply take a break. These consequences affect more than the individual’s schedule; they influence relationships and participation in working life.

Employers can improve the situation by reviewing workloads and making expectations about contact hours clear. A formal right to leave work is of little use if employees are still expected to answer routine messages throughout the evening. Managers should therefore plan tasks realistically and respect agreed boundaries. At home, family members can discuss the division of domestic responsibilities and adjust it to their circumstances. Sharing recurring tasks can protect time for rest and prevent one person’s career from being consistently treated as less important. Flexible working arrangements may help where they support these practical changes.

In conclusion, poor work life balance can undermine relationships, recovery and career opportunities. Reasonable employment expectations and a fairer distribution of household responsibilities address these problems together. Successful change requires boundaries that people can actually maintain in everyday life.
Check the answer

Problems and solutions. Discuss consequences, rather than using the whole first paragraph for causes. Limit: A pay rise alone may not reduce excessive hours. Vocabulary: support network; household responsibilities; career development.
P5 Less family time
Task: People are spending less time with their family members. What are the reasons for this phenomenon? What effects does it have?
Suggested complete response | 287 words

Family members in some households have fewer opportunities to spend time together. Conflicting schedules and individual use of digital entertainment help explain this change. Its effects can include weaker emotional support and fewer chances for children to receive everyday guidance, although the outcome depends on how families maintain contact.

The first reason is that work and study commitments often occur at different times. Parents may return home late, while children have lessons or assignments that occupy their evenings. Even when everyone lives in the same house, finding a period for a shared meal can be difficult. A second reason is that available leisure time may be spent separately on screens. Someone watching videos or exchanging messages with distant friends may pay little attention to relatives nearby. Technology can certainly connect family members who live apart, but it can also displace conversation when it becomes the default activity during time that could be shared.

Reduced interaction can make it harder for relatives to notice when someone needs support. A problem at school or work may remain unspoken if there is rarely a relaxed opportunity to talk. Children may also have fewer chances to observe how adults deal with disagreements or responsibilities. Such learning often happens through ordinary routines rather than formal advice. However, less time together does not automatically mean that a family is uncaring. Short but attentive conversations and regular shared activities may preserve strong relationships. The quality of interaction therefore matters alongside its frequency.

In conclusion, busy schedules and separate digital routines can reduce shared family time. This may weaken support and everyday learning if meaningful contact is lost. The most serious effects arise when limited time is accompanied by limited attention to one another’s needs.
Check the answer

Reasons and effects. Keep the causal chain visible. Limit: Online communication can also help relatives who live apart. Vocabulary: family bonding (gắn kết gia đình); competing priorities; emotional support.
P6 Fair university access

Task: Some people think everyone has the right to access university education and governments should provide places for all students, no matter their financial background. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Suggested complete response | 289 words

A person’s financial background should not decide whether they can attend university. I largely agree that governments should support fair access to places. However, this should mean removing financial barriers for suitable applicants, rather than assuming that every person must enter a university regardless of their preparation or interests.

The strongest reason for public support is that cost can prevent capable students from continuing their education. An applicant from a low income household may meet admission requirements but struggle to pay tuition or living expenses. If the opportunity is lost solely because of money, both the student and society may miss the benefits of their potential. Grants, affordable student support and suitable accommodation can reduce these barriers. For example, assistance with living costs may be as important as tuition support for someone who must move away from home. Fair access requires attention to the actual expenses that prevent participation.

Nevertheless, governments also need to consider educational capacity and suitability. University courses require resources and appropriate prior preparation, so providing a place without support or relevant prerequisites may not lead to successful study. Some people also prefer vocational training or employment routes that match their goals more closely. These choices should receive serious support rather than be presented as inferior alternatives. Governments can expand opportunities while maintaining clear admission standards and investing in several forms of further education. This approach respects the right to pursue learning without treating university as the only worthwhile destination.

In conclusion, financial circumstances should not exclude eligible students from higher education, and governments have an important role in making access fair. The policy should combine practical financial support with suitable places and alternative pathways, so that opportunity reflects ability and interests rather than household income.
Check the answer

Opinion. Possible view: Support access based on ability and interest, without financial exclusion. Limit: Financially fair access is not automatically universal free tuition or admission without prerequisites. Vocabulary: financial background; eligibility; targeted support.
P7 Internet access and achievement
Task: Internet access helps young people and workers achieve their education and work goals more easily than before. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Suggested complete response | 287 words

Internet access has made many educational and professional goals easier to pursue. I largely agree with this view because online resources broaden learning opportunities and digital communication reduces barriers to collaboration. However, these advantages depend on reliable access, relevant skills and the ability to manage distractions.

For learners, the internet provides access to explanations, courses and practice materials beyond those available locally. A student who does not understand a classroom explanation can revisit the topic through another presentation and work at a suitable pace. This can be especially helpful when a specialist subject is not offered nearby. Search tools also make it easier to locate information for projects, although students must assess its reliability. The advantage is therefore more than simply obtaining material quickly: learners can choose resources that match their needs and return to them when necessary. Effective use still requires active practice rather than passive viewing.

Workers benefit from easier communication across distances. Colleagues can share files, discuss a proposal in a video meeting and coordinate a project without travelling to the same office. These possibilities reduce some time and transport costs and make it easier to involve people with different expertise. Nevertheless, being connected does not guarantee success. Frequent notifications can interrupt concentrated work, while unreliable connections may make remote participation difficult. Digital skills and clear working routines are therefore needed to turn access into an actual improvement. People without suitable devices or connections may gain less than others.

In conclusion, the internet has expanded opportunities to learn and collaborate, making many goals more achievable than before. I agree with the general claim, while recognising that the benefits are conditional. Access is most useful when combined with sound judgement, practical skills and purposeful use.
Check the answer

Opinion. Possible view: Largely agree, while recognising unequal access and distractions. Limit: Access creates opportunities; it does not guarantee success or equal outcomes. Vocabulary: remote collaboration; digital skills; flexible learning.
P8 Violence on screens
Task: Violence on TV and in films is harmful, so governments should ban it. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Suggested complete response | 284 words

Violent scenes in films and television can be disturbing, especially for younger viewers. However, I disagree that recognising possible harm necessarily justifies banning all such content. Age appropriate restrictions and effective supervision offer a more focused response while allowing adults to make informed viewing choices.

There are legitimate concerns about children’s exposure to graphic violence. Some scenes may cause distress, and repeated portrayals of aggression without consequences can give an incomplete picture of how conflicts should be handled. Younger viewers may need help distinguishing dramatic entertainment from acceptable behaviour in everyday life. These concerns deserve attention, but they do not establish that every violent scene has the same effect on every audience. Context matters: a film may portray suffering critically rather than celebrate it. A complete prohibition would remove this distinction and treat very different forms of storytelling as equally harmful.

A better approach is to make access and presentation suitable for the intended audience. Clear age ratings can help parents choose programmes, while parental controls can restrict children’s access to unsuitable material. Broadcasters and platforms can also provide meaningful warnings and apply appropriate limits to particularly graphic scenes. Adults who want to watch a serious film about conflict would then retain that choice, while children receive greater protection. These measures require practical enforcement and parental attention, because a label alone may not prevent access. Schools and families can further support critical discussion of what young people watch.

In conclusion, screen violence can raise valid concerns, but a blanket ban is too broad a response. Targeted restrictions, supervision and guidance address the risks more directly. They recognise differences in audience and context while preserving the ability to discuss difficult subjects through film and television.
Check the answer

Two linked claims. Possible view: Accept possible harm, but reject a blanket ban. Limit: Recognising harm does not prove that complete prohibition is necessary. Vocabulary: graphic violence; impressionable (dễ bị ảnh hưởng); parental supervision.
P9 Technology and all societies
Task: Modern technology is transforming how we work and is of benefit to all societies. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Suggested complete response | 297 words

Modern technology is changing the way many people work, from communication to manufacturing. I agree that this transformation is widespread, but I do not accept that it benefits all societies equally or automatically. The gains depend on access, skills and how the costs of change are managed.

Digital communication has made it easier for colleagues in different places to collaborate. A team can discuss a design through video meetings and share updated documents without arranging international travel. Automation can also take over repetitive tasks, allowing workers to focus on supervision or quality checks. These changes may improve efficiency and reduce some physically demanding work. They demonstrate why technology can bring substantial benefits, particularly where organisations have the equipment and expertise needed to use it effectively. However, a new system is valuable only if it fits the task and operates reliably, rather than being adopted simply because it is fashionable.

The claim of benefit to all societies needs more qualification. Some communities lack reliable electricity, connectivity or training, which limits their ability to use advanced systems. Installing equipment without the skills to maintain it can create expense without lasting improvement. Workers whose tasks are automated may also need retraining and support to find other roles. If these needs are ignored, the gains may be concentrated among employers or already skilled workers while others face insecurity. Governments and organisations therefore have a role in widening access and preparing people for changing work, rather than assuming that benefits will spread by themselves.

In conclusion, technology is transforming work and can offer major advantages. Yet its effects differ across societies and groups within them. I agree with the first part of the statement, while rejecting an unqualified claim of universal benefit unless the conditions for useful and inclusive adoption are addressed.
Check the answer

Two claims. Possible view: Agree that work is changing, but qualify the claim of universal benefit. Limit: Address “all societies” explicitly. Avoid claiming that a single tool solves every professional problem. Vocabulary: automation; retraining; unequal access.
P10 Roads and public transport
Task: Some people think it is more important to spend money on roads and motorways than on public transport systems. To what extent do you agree?
Suggested complete response | 296 words

Public investment in transport must meet different needs, and roads as well as public transport require funding. I disagree that roads and motorways should always receive greater priority. In congested cities, improving public transport often offers wider benefits, while essential road maintenance should still be protected.

Road investment has clear value when it addresses safety and necessary access. Damaged surfaces, unclear markings and difficult junctions can create problems for drivers, pedestrians and cyclists. Maintaining roads also supports buses, deliveries and emergency vehicles, so this spending benefits more than private car owners. In some rural areas, road connections may be particularly important because population patterns make frequent public transport difficult to provide. These considerations justify continued funding. However, expanding roads is a different decision from keeping them safe: additional capacity may attract more journeys and does not always provide a lasting answer to congestion.

In a crowded city, reliable public transport can move many people without requiring each traveller to use a separate vehicle. Frequent services and convenient connections make it easier for residents to consider alternatives to driving. Affordable fares also help students, low income workers and people who cannot drive. For example, a well connected bus route can make employment accessible without the cost of owning a car. These benefits give public transport a strong claim on urban budgets. Investment should improve the whole journey, including walking access and transfers, because a comfortable vehicle alone is insufficient if the service is difficult to reach or rarely available.

In conclusion, safe roads remain necessary, but the argument for giving them greater importance in every setting is unconvincing. Spending should reflect local needs. In congested urban areas, public transport can deserve priority because it offers efficient mobility and broader access, alongside continued maintenance of the road network.
Check the answer

Comparison. Possible view: Maintain safe roads, but prioritise public transport in congested cities. Limit: Wider roads may attract additional traffic; neither type of investment fits every location. Vocabulary: congestion (ùn tắc); road maintenance; transit networks.
P11 Old buildings
Task: Many people think old buildings should be knocked down to give way to new buildings. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Suggested complete response | 303 words

Some people favour replacing old buildings with new developments. I disagree with demolition as a general policy based simply on age. The decision should reflect safety, historical value and the possibility of adapting a building to current needs, rather than assume that all older structures have become unnecessary.

Many old buildings preserve features that would be difficult to replace. Their materials, craftsmanship and layout can reveal aspects of local history and contribute to a place’s distinctive character. A historic market or public building may also attract visitors and support nearby businesses. Where possible, restoration or reuse can retain these benefits while allowing the structure to serve a new purpose. For example, an unused industrial building might become a library or community space if the conversion is practical. Such projects show that preservation need not prevent development. The important question is whether the building’s value can be maintained through a suitable use.

Nevertheless, some older buildings may be unsafe or difficult to adapt. A structure with serious damage and little historical importance could require repairs that are disproportionate to its public benefit. Replacing it may provide safer housing or more accessible facilities. This is a reason for careful assessment, however, rather than permission to clear every old property. Authorities and owners should compare repair costs, functional needs and the effect on residents and surrounding streets. Public consultation may also identify values that are not obvious from a financial estimate alone. A new building should offer a clear improvement rather than merely a different appearance.

In conclusion, neither age nor the prospect of a modern replacement is sufficient to justify demolition. Valuable buildings should be preserved or adapted where feasible, while unsafe and unsuitable structures may be replaced after assessment. This balanced approach allows cities to meet present needs without unnecessarily losing their architectural heritage.
Check the answer

Opinion. Possible view: Assess buildings individually rather than demolishing them solely because of age. Limit: Old does not always mean unsafe, and new does not always mean better. Vocabulary: cultural heritage; restoration; craftsmanship (tay nghề thủ công).
P12 Moving companies to the countryside
Task: Traffic and housing problems could only be solved by moving large companies, factories and their employees to the countryside. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Suggested complete response | 296 words

Relocating large businesses and factories to rural areas may reduce some pressures on cities. However, I disagree that it is the only way to solve traffic and housing problems. Relocation has limits, and improvements to urban transport and housing can address these issues without moving every workplace.

There are potential benefits when jobs and employees leave a congested area. Fewer daily commuters may reduce pressure on busy routes, and lower demand for accommodation could ease competition for some homes. The receiving area may also gain employment and investment. Nevertheless, these outcomes depend on how relocation is organised. Employees who remain in the city could face longer journeys, while rural communities may experience new housing and traffic pressures. Moving a factory does not by itself provide suitable homes, transport links or services in its new location. The policy can therefore transfer difficulties unless it is supported by careful planning.

Cities also have alternatives that address the causes more directly. Reliable public transport can reduce dependence on private vehicles, while staggered work schedules may spread demand across the day. Housing policies can encourage appropriate development near jobs and services, reducing the need for long commutes. For example, making an existing neighbourhood more accessible by bus may improve travel without requiring residents or businesses to move away. Affordable housing programmes can also target households whose needs are not met by the market. These measures require resources and coordination, but they demonstrate that relocation is one possible tool among several rather than the sole solution.

In conclusion, moving some workplaces may help where city pressures are severe and receiving areas are prepared. Yet traffic and housing problems can also be addressed through better transport, appropriate housing supply and improved urban planning. The word “only” makes the proposed solution too restrictive.
Check the answer

An “only” claim. Possible view: Relocation may help, but it is not the sole solution. Limit: Explain how alternatives work, not simply that they exist. Vocabulary: relocation; urban planning (quy hoạch đô thị); housing supply.
P13 The purpose of sport
Task: Many people believe that sports are only a form of recreation. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Suggested complete response | 287 words

Sport is often enjoyed as a form of recreation, but I disagree that this is its only purpose. Participation can also develop physical skills, discipline and cooperation. These benefits help explain why sporting activities have a place in education and community life as well as leisure.

One contribution beyond entertainment is the opportunity to practise sustained physical activity and improve particular skills. A swimmer, for example, needs to develop technique through repeated training rather than rely entirely on enthusiasm. Following a routine and responding to feedback can encourage persistence. These habits may remain useful outside sport because progress often requires patience and realistic goals. The benefits are not automatic: unsuitable training or excessive pressure can reduce enjoyment and create problems. Nevertheless, well organised participation can provide a structured setting for learning how effort, recovery and gradual improvement work together.

Sport can also develop relationships and shared responsibilities. In a team game, players must communicate, respect rules and coordinate their actions. A talented individual cannot always succeed if the group fails to work together. Community events may further bring people from different backgrounds into contact through a common activity. Even an individual sport can involve coaches, training partners and clubs, so its social value should not be overlooked. These experiences demonstrate that sporting participation can involve learning and belonging, not merely passing time pleasantly. Enjoyment may make these activities more attractive, but it does not exhaust their purpose.

In conclusion, recreation is an important part of sport, yet describing it as the only role leaves out several valuable contributions. Physical learning, discipline and cooperation can all develop through suitable participation. Recognising these wider purposes supports opportunities for sport that are enjoyable, accessible and appropriate to the people involved.
Check the answer

An “only” claim. Possible view: Disagree because sport has purposes beyond entertainment. Limit: Acknowledge enjoyment; the disagreement concerns the word “only”. Vocabulary: recreation; discipline; community participation.
P14 Financial aid and practical assistance

Task: Some people think developing countries need financial help from international governments and organisations. Others think practical aid and advice are needed. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Suggested complete response | 296 words

Developing countries may receive international assistance in the form of money, practical resources or advice. Financial help can address immediate resource gaps, while technical support can improve the use of available resources. In my view, neither should be treated as universally superior; an appropriate combination usually offers the strongest approach.

Those who favour financial assistance point out that many projects cannot proceed without funding. Building a water system, for example, involves paying for equipment, materials and workers, not merely identifying a suitable design. Money can also allow local organisations to choose priorities that reflect their circumstances. However, weak oversight or unclear objectives may reduce the benefit of a transfer. Funds need transparent management and realistic plans, while the terms of assistance should be understood. Not every payment is a loan, but where repayment is required, the future burden must be considered. Financial support is useful when it addresses a genuine need and can be managed responsibly.

Practical aid and advice can contribute in different ways. Training enables local workers to maintain equipment, and specialist knowledge may help organisations avoid costly mistakes. Yet advice that ignores local conditions can be difficult to apply. A technically advanced proposal may fail where the necessary equipment or maintenance capacity is unavailable. This is why I favour combining support with local participation. Funding can provide essential resources, while training and consultation help ensure that the project can continue after outside experts leave. Recipients should take part in decisions rather than simply implement a standard plan developed elsewhere.

In conclusion, money and practical expertise respond to different constraints. Effective assistance should identify what a community needs and combine resources accordingly. Locally appropriate planning, financial support and capacity building are more convincing than insisting on one form of aid for every developing country.
Check the answer

Discussion. Possible view: Combine funding with locally appropriate expertise. Limit: The best mix depends on the problem and local capacity. Vocabulary: financial assistance; technical expertise; recipient country.
P15 Team and individual sports
Task: Some people think team sports, like football, are more beneficial for children. Others prefer individual sports, like tennis or swimming. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Suggested complete response | 291 words

Some parents believe children benefit most from team sports, while others prefer individual activities. Both views have merit because the activities can develop different skills. I believe children should have opportunities to try both, with the final choice reflecting their interests and the quality of the available coaching.

Team sports provide a clear setting for practising cooperation. Players need to communicate, understand their roles and respond to what others are doing. In football, for example, an effective pass may contribute more to the team than an individual attempt to score. Children can learn that success depends on shared effort and that mistakes need a constructive response. Training and competition also create opportunities for friendship with teammates. These benefits help explain why many parents value group activities. However, they depend on an environment where coaches encourage respect and participation rather than allow a few stronger players to dominate everyone else.

Individual sports can place greater emphasis on personal progress. A child learning to swim may set a manageable goal, practise a technique and observe improvement over time. Responsibility for that progress can develop self discipline and confidence. Individual activities may also suit children who prefer concentrating on their own performance. Nevertheless, they do not necessarily involve isolation: instructors, training partners and clubs often provide social contact. I therefore see the two categories as complementary. Access to a range of activities lets children discover what they enjoy and gain different experiences, without assuming that one format provides every benefit.

In conclusion, team sports can strengthen cooperation and belonging, while individual sports can support independence and focused improvement. Neither is automatically better for every child. A varied programme with supportive coaching gives children the best opportunity to choose suitable activities and develop through participation.
Check the answer

Discussion. Possible view: Both are valuable; suitability depends on the child and the setting. Limit: Do not assume individual sports involve no coaches, teammates or social contact. Vocabulary: teamwork; self discipline; personal progress.
P16 Food travelling long distances
Task: Today food travels thousands of miles before it reaches customers. Why is this? Is this a positive or negative trend?
Suggested complete response | 298 words

Food is often transported over long distances before it reaches consumers. Demand for a wider variety of products and the organisation of international trade help explain this pattern. I regard it as largely positive because it broadens access to food, although transport costs and effects on local producers require attention.

One reason for long distance trade is that not every region can produce the same foods throughout the year. Consumers may want fruit outside its local growing season or ingredients that are associated with another climate. Businesses respond by buying from places where these products are available. Trade networks, refrigeration and distribution systems make such exchanges practical on a large scale. Demand for different cuisines also encourages suppliers to import specialist foods. These factors explain why the journey reflects both consumer preferences and differences in production, rather than simply a desire to transport food as far as possible.

The main benefit is greater choice and a more varied supply. Imports may help a region obtain food when local production is limited, while exporters gain access to customers beyond their own market. Consumers can therefore benefit from products that would otherwise be unavailable or difficult to obtain. Nevertheless, the advantages come with costs. Transport and storage require resources, and some local farmers may face difficult competition. These concerns justify careful supply decisions and support for producers adapting to changing markets. Distance alone does not determine environmental impact, since production methods matter as well. Comparing the whole supply process is more useful than assuming that all imported food is necessarily worse.

In conclusion, long distance food trade is driven by demand, production differences and distribution systems. Its contribution to choice and supply makes it generally beneficial, provided that environmental costs and local economic effects are taken seriously rather than overlooked.
Check the answer

Two part question. Possible view: Benefits are substantial, but impacts depend on production and transport. Limit: Distance alone does not determine a food’s total environmental impact. Vocabulary: food security; trade barriers; transportation; local producers.
P17 Traditional dress and the past
Task: Traditional dress and costumes are considered effective ways of maintaining links with the past. How effective can they be? What other ways help citizens connect with a country’s past?
Suggested complete response | 301 words

Traditional clothing can make a country’s connection with the past visible, especially during cultural events. However, its effectiveness depends on whether people understand the history and practices associated with it. Museums, family stories and education can deepen that understanding and provide links that clothing alone cannot establish.

Traditional dress can be effective because it turns cultural identity into something people can see and participate in. Wearing or observing an áo dài at a Vietnamese celebration, for example, may encourage discussion of design, craftsmanship and the ways clothing has changed over time. Such experiences can create an interest that a purely abstract explanation might not produce. Yet the connection may remain superficial if an outfit is worn without any understanding of its context. People could recognise the appearance while knowing little about the communities, occasions or traditions associated with it. Clothing is therefore a useful starting point rather than a complete form of historical education.

Other methods can supply the context that visual symbols lack. Museums can place clothing and other objects alongside accounts of how people lived, helping visitors connect an item to a wider period or event. School lessons can explain major developments and encourage students to compare sources, while conversations with older relatives can preserve memories of everyday practices. Community workshops may also allow people to learn a traditional craft directly. These approaches are particularly valuable when they recognise regional variation, rather than suggest that one garment represents every person in a country. Together, they make the connection more detailed and meaningful.

In conclusion, traditional costumes can maintain links with the past by creating visible and memorable cultural experiences. Their effectiveness increases when they are accompanied by explanation. Museums, education, oral histories and practical activities provide complementary ways for citizens to understand the people and traditions behind those symbols.
Check the answer

Two questions. Evaluate effectiveness, then explain other methods. Limit: Avoid presenting one costume as representing every person in a country. Vocabulary: cultural identity; artefacts; historical understanding.
P18 Natural extinction and conservation
Task: It is a natural process for animal species to become extinct. There is no reason why people should try to prevent this. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Suggested complete response | 297 words

Animal species have disappeared through natural processes, but this does not remove the reasons for conservation. I agree that extinction can occur without human involvement. However, I strongly disagree that people should therefore make no effort to prevent avoidable losses caused or accelerated by their own activities.

Natural changes in environmental conditions can make survival difficult for some species. Over long periods, habitats and relationships between organisms change, and not every population can adapt successfully. Recognising this helps avoid the unrealistic expectation that every species can be preserved forever in an unchanged environment. Nevertheless, human activities introduce additional pressures that should be considered separately. Clearing habitats, polluting living environments or taking animals at unsustainable rates can reduce populations in ways that are not simply unavoidable natural change. Calling extinction natural does not explain away these actions or establish that preventing their effects would be pointless.

Conservation is justified because it can reduce harm over which people have some control. Protecting breeding areas or limiting exploitation can give a threatened population a better chance to recover. Maintaining species may also protect ecological relationships on which other organisms and communities depend. For example, preserving a habitat can support several connected populations rather than benefit only one animal. Conservation decisions still need to consider available resources and the likelihood of success. However, those practical limits are reasons to set priorities, not evidence that there is no reason to act at all. Preventing avoidable damage remains a meaningful objective even when universal protection is impossible.

In conclusion, natural extinction is part of environmental history, but it does not justify indifference to human caused losses. People should address pressures they can reduce and protect important habitats and relationships. Accepting that some change is inevitable is compatible with taking responsibility for avoidable harm.
Check the answer

Two linked claims. Possible view: Natural extinction occurs, but that does not remove reasons for conservation. Limit: Do not assume every extinction strengthens an ecosystem. Vocabulary: extinction (tuyệt chủng); endangered species; ecological balance.
P19 Economic growth and a clean environment
Task: Some people say a country can be both economically successful and have a clean environment. Others disagree. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Suggested complete response | 298 words

Economic success and environmental protection are sometimes presented as competing goals. There are real tensions when growth relies on polluting activities, but I believe the two can coexist. Achieving this requires effective standards and investment rather than assuming that either growth or environmental quality will automatically produce the other.

Those who see an unavoidable conflict point to the resources used in production and development. Factories may consume energy and release waste, while construction can place pressure on land and habitats. Preventing these effects involves costs that businesses and public authorities may struggle to meet. A firm replacing equipment or installing treatment systems may face a significant initial expense. These concerns explain why some people regard environmental rules as an obstacle to economic activity, particularly where institutions have limited resources. They also show why the transition cannot be achieved merely by announcing ambitious targets without a workable plan.

However, the existence of costs does not mean a clean environment and a successful economy are fundamentally incompatible. More efficient equipment can reduce the materials or energy needed for a particular output, while proper waste treatment can allow activity to continue with less damage. Businesses may also develop products and services that support cleaner systems. Governments can help through clear requirements, infrastructure and appropriately designed support for change. For example, coordinated investment may make it easier for several small businesses to use suitable waste facilities. Progress will differ between sectors, but these possibilities demonstrate that prosperity need not depend permanently on the most damaging practices.

In conclusion, economic development can create environmental pressure, and reducing that pressure involves genuine challenges. Nevertheless, the goals can coexist where investment, regulation and production choices are aligned. A successful policy should manage the transition realistically rather than accept pollution as an unavoidable condition of prosperity.
Check the answer

Discussion. Possible view: The goals can coexist, but require effective policy and investment. Limit: Economic growth does not automatically finance protection or eliminate pollution. Vocabulary: environmental sustainability; trade off; cleaner production.
P20 Global warming and deforestation
Task: Some people believe global warming is today’s most pressing environmental problem. Others consider deforestation to have the most devastating impact. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Suggested complete response | 310 words

Global warming and deforestation both deserve urgent attention, and the two problems are connected. Some people emphasise the worldwide reach of climate change, while others point to the immediate damage caused by forest loss. In my view, global warming has broader consequences, but addressing it should include strong efforts to protect forests.

Deforestation can have severe effects on the places where it occurs. Removing forests destroys habitats and may disrupt the livelihoods of communities that depend on them. It can also reduce the environmental functions that trees and surrounding ecosystems provide. These consequences explain why someone living near a threatened forest may regard clearance as the most pressing problem. Protection is not as simple as passing a local rule: monitoring, economic incentives and alternatives for affected communities may all be needed. The immediate nature of the damage therefore gives this view considerable strength, even when the effects are not identical in every location.

The argument for prioritising global warming rests on the breadth and duration of its effects. A changing climate can influence conditions across many regions and affect agriculture, infrastructure and ecosystems together. Responses also require cooperation because the causes and consequences cross national boundaries. This wider reach makes the issue especially significant in my judgement. However, choosing it as the greater overall priority should not imply that forest protection is secondary in every decision. Forest loss and climate pressures can reinforce one another, so treating them as entirely separate problems creates a misleading choice. Measures should address their connections as well as their distinct effects.

In conclusion, deforestation causes serious and sometimes immediate damage, while global warming presents a broader challenge across regions and systems. I consider climate change the greater overall priority, but an effective response must include forest protection. Comparing urgency is useful only if it leads to coordinated action rather than neglect of either problem.
Check the answer

Discussion and comparison. Possible view: Climate change has broader effects, while forest protection remains essential. Limit: Do not dismiss deforestation as minor or suggest a local law alone solves it. Vocabulary: forest clearance; habitat protection; climate impacts.
P21 Who should solve environmental problems
Task: Solving environmental problems should be the responsibility of an international organisation rather than each national government. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Suggested complete response | 295 words

Environmental problems often cross borders, making international cooperation necessary. However, I disagree that responsibility should rest with an international organisation instead of national governments. International coordination and domestic implementation perform different roles, and both are needed for environmental measures to have a practical effect.

International bodies can help countries address problems that cannot be managed effectively through isolated action. They provide places to negotiate common goals, exchange knowledge and coordinate support. A country with fewer resources may benefit from assistance in developing cleaner infrastructure, while shared monitoring can make progress easier to compare. Cooperation is also valuable when activities in one region affect people elsewhere. These advantages justify a substantial international role. Nevertheless, an agreement does not automatically determine every local action or provide the staff and resources needed to enforce it. Coordination must be connected to institutions capable of carrying out the commitments.

National and local authorities are essential for that implementation. They can establish operating rules, inspect facilities and adapt policies to particular conditions. A coastal community managing wastewater faces different immediate needs from an inland area protecting forests. Governments also influence public infrastructure and services that shape everyday behaviour. For example, an international commitment to reduce environmental pressure may require domestic investment in reliable public transport before residents have a practical alternative to driving. Local participation matters as well, because policies are more workable when people understand what they are expected to do. Removing national responsibility would weaken these links between general aims and concrete changes.

In conclusion, international organisations can support cooperation, common objectives and resource sharing. National governments remain responsible for turning these commitments into rules, services and enforcement appropriate to their circumstances. Environmental protection is best served by shared responsibility rather than replacing one level of action with another.
Check the answer

Comparison. Possible view: Responsibility should be shared. Limit: Avoid treating international bodies as a single authority able to enforce every local decision. Vocabulary: international cooperation; local implementation; monitoring.
P22 Children becoming overweight
Task: In many countries, children are becoming overweight and unhealthy. Some people think the government should have responsibility for solving this problem. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Suggested complete response | 300 words

Governments have an important responsibility to support children’s health, including addressing conditions that contribute to unhealthy routines. I agree with this principle, but I do not believe public authorities can solve the problem alone. Families and schools must also act because they influence children’s daily meals and activities directly.

Government involvement is justified where individual households cannot supply the systems they need. Public authorities can improve access to safe parks, walking routes and affordable recreation facilities. They can also support clear food information and standards in services used by children. For example, a neighbourhood without safe outdoor space makes regular activity more difficult even when parents want to encourage it. Public investment can change that environment and create opportunities for many households at once. These actions show why responsibility cannot simply be assigned to individual choice. The choices available are partly shaped by infrastructure and public policy.

Nevertheless, government action needs support from the people who spend time with children each day. Parents influence the meals available at home and the balance between screen use and other activities. Schools organise routines that can include active play and practical education about healthy habits. These everyday decisions help translate public provision into actual participation. A new sports facility provides little benefit to a child who never has an opportunity to use it. Cooperation also allows different barriers to be recognised, such as cost, time or access. Measures should support families in making workable changes rather than assume that every household faces the same circumstances.

In conclusion, governments should accept an important role in creating conditions that support children’s health. Yet parents and schools have equally necessary roles in everyday practice. Shared action is more convincing than expecting public policy alone to determine children’s habits or placing the whole burden on individual families.
Check the answer

Opinion about responsibility. Possible view: Government has an important role, alongside families and schools. Limit: Do not spend a whole paragraph proving that children are overweight; answer who should act. Vocabulary: healthy habits; public facilities; shared responsibility.
P23 Exercise in cities
Task: It is difficult for people in cities to get enough physical exercise. What are the causes and solutions?
Suggested complete response | 301 words

People living in cities may struggle to fit sufficient physical activity into their routines. Demanding schedules and inconvenient or unsuitable spaces are two important barriers. Solutions should therefore make activity easier to include in everyday life, rather than rely only on telling residents that exercise is valuable.

Long commutes and work commitments can leave people with little free time. Someone who spends much of the day travelling and working may find a separate journey to a sports facility difficult to maintain. The built environment can create another obstacle. In some neighbourhoods, walking routes are uncomfortable or disconnected, while nearby spaces for recreation may be limited. These barriers can affect people differently depending on their schedules, income and mobility. They help explain why motivation alone is insufficient: a person may want to be active but still lack a convenient opportunity. Expensive private facilities are not a practical solution for every resident.

Employers and city authorities can address these constraints through complementary measures. Reasonable schedules and opportunities for short active breaks may help workers avoid remaining seated for the whole day. Authorities can improve connected walking routes, suitable cycling links and accessible public parks. When activity becomes part of a journey people already make, it requires less additional time. For example, a safe route between homes and local services may encourage residents to walk for routine errands. Facilities also need maintenance and convenient access, because constructing a park in an isolated location may do little for those with limited time. Solutions should reflect how residents actually use the city.

In conclusion, time pressure and an environment that makes activity inconvenient can limit exercise in cities. Better schedules, active travel routes and accessible recreation spaces address these barriers directly. Practical opportunities are essential if advice about healthy routines is to lead to lasting change.
Check the answer

Causes and solutions. Pair time barriers with practical changes. Limit: Avoid assuming that indoor exercise is inherently unsafe or that everyone can afford a gym. Vocabulary: city dwellers; accessible facilities; active travel.
P24 Good news and bad news
Task: The media should include more stories reporting good news rather than bad news. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Suggested complete response | 289 words

The media can provide valuable stories about achievements and constructive responses to problems. I support giving such news greater attention, but I disagree that positive stories should generally replace negative ones. Public importance and accuracy should guide coverage, whether the events being reported are encouraging or troubling.

Positive news can help readers see possibilities for useful action. A report about a successful community project may explain how residents organised support and what others could learn from it. Coverage of practical improvements can also balance a stream of alarming headlines, making the picture of society more complete. These stories deserve space when they are relevant and properly investigated. However, positive reporting should involve more than presenting an optimistic message. Journalists should examine limitations and explain the evidence for success, so that a pleasing story remains informative rather than becoming promotion without scrutiny.

Negative news has a different but equally important role. Reporting disasters can help people respond to danger, while investigation of abuse or corruption may reveal problems that institutions would otherwise ignore. Removing such stories merely because they are upsetting would leave the public less informed. The issue is often how a story is presented: sensational headlines and unnecessary disturbing detail can attract attention without improving understanding. Responsible reporting can describe serious harm accurately and consider its causes and possible responses. This approach combines accountability with constructive information, instead of forcing a choice between constant alarm and uncritical optimism.

In conclusion, the media should include more worthwhile positive stories where they improve public understanding. Nevertheless, coverage of serious problems remains essential. I favour a broader and more responsible mix of news, selected for its relevance and evidence rather than a simple preference for events that make readers feel good.
Check the answer

Opinion. Possible view: Support more constructive reporting while keeping coverage of serious problems. Limit: Distinguish necessary negative news from sensational treatment. Vocabulary: balanced coverage; public interest; sensational headlines.
P25 Newspapers and other media
Task: Some people think newspapers are the best way to get news. Others believe other media platforms are better. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Suggested complete response | 300 words

People can obtain news through newspapers, broadcast services and digital platforms, each with particular strengths. Some prefer newspapers for detailed reporting, while others value the convenience and speed of other formats. I believe the best choice depends on the reader’s purpose, with reliability being more important than the medium itself.

Newspapers can offer a focused selection of stories with background and editorial organisation. A reader may find it easier to consider a detailed article when it is presented without constant notifications or competing short posts. Editorial checks can also help clarify complex information and provide context beyond an immediate update. These features explain why some people regard newspapers as the strongest source. However, they are not guarantees of accuracy, and newspapers differ in their standards and priorities. Many also publish online, so the value often lies in the reporting organisation and its methods rather than paper as a physical format.

Other media platforms can be more suitable when information needs to reach people quickly. Broadcasts and digital services can provide updates, maps or video that help explain a developing event. They may also be easier to access during travel or for readers who prefer listening. The challenge is that fast circulation can allow unreliable claims to spread alongside verified information. Users should therefore consider who produced a report and whether it has been checked. A credible digital publication may be more useful than a poorly reported newspaper, just as a careful newspaper investigation may offer more context than a brief social media post.

In conclusion, newspapers provide advantages in depth and focused reading, while other platforms offer speed and varied presentation. No format is best for every situation. Readers should choose suitable media while prioritising transparent reporting, verification and context, rather than assume that reliability follows automatically from the format.
Check the answer

Discussion. Possible view: Evaluate reliability and purpose, rather than assuming one format is always best. Limit: Newspapers may publish online, so distinguish format from the organisation producing the news. Vocabulary: editorial standards; credibility; verification.
First essay answer on food waste

Answer to the full essay exercise in the Write your first complete essay section and planning worksheet in the Plan before you write section. Attempt the task first, then compare how the causes and solutions are matched.
Task: Nowadays, people tend to waste a great amount of food. Why is this happening, and how can we solve this problem?
Suggested complete response | 280 words

A considerable amount of food is purchased or prepared but never eaten. Two avoidable causes are poor planning before shopping and serving portions that are too large. More careful purchasing and greater flexibility over portion sizes could help reduce this waste.

Poor planning often leads households to buy more perishable food than they can use. Shoppers who do not check their cupboards may purchase items they already have, while special offers can encourage them to buy quantities that exceed their needs. Some of this food then spoils before it is eaten. Oversized portions create a similar problem after food has been prepared. At home or in a restaurant, people may serve a standard large amount without considering an individual’s appetite. If the remaining food is discarded rather than stored safely or shared, the ingredients and effort used to prepare it are wasted.

The solutions should address these two stages directly. Before shopping, households can check existing supplies and plan a realistic number of meals. A list based on those meals makes it easier to avoid unnecessary purchases, although it should allow for changes in plans. People can also serve smaller initial portions and offer more food when needed. Restaurants could support this approach by providing different portion sizes, allowing customers to choose an amount they are likely to finish. These actions do not require everyone to follow an identical diet; they simply bring the quantity purchased or served closer to the quantity actually needed.

In conclusion, food waste is often connected to decisions made before shopping and before serving a meal. Checking supplies, planning purchases and offering suitable portions can reduce these avoidable losses by dealing with their immediate causes.
Check the answer
Each solution matches a cause: shopping lists address overbuying, and flexible portions address uneaten servings. The conclusion adds no new solution.

theory.text: Theory & skills required

Matching Information asks which paragraph contains a given piece of information. Matching Features connects statements with a named person, place or other category. Check whether letters may be used more than once.
Key skills: Scanning names and concepts; matching paraphrased relationships.

guide.text: Planning guide
Identify what must be matched  scan for distinctive terms or names  read contextual evidence  check meaning, not just keywords  follow reuse instructions.

small.text: Small exercise
A. Dr Lin measured rainfall. B. Dr Rao compared soil samples. C. Dr Park designed water sensors.
Match the descriptions with A–C: E1. developed measuring equipment; E2. studied soil; E3. collected precipitation data.

full.text: Full exercise A — Matching Information
Reading passage

A. In 2015, the city converted an unused railway line into a footpath for commuting and exercise.B. In 2018, engineers installed rain gardens beside streets to absorb stormwater.C. In 2021, a university surveyed cyclists and pedestrians about which routes felt safest.
Which paragraph contains the following information?1. A study of users’ perceptions2. An old transport route put to a new use3. A method of managing excess rainfall
Full exercise B — Matching Features
Reading passage

Dr Amelia Green studied how trees could reduce temperatures in crowded city centres. Her findings suggested that shaded streets stayed cooler in summer.Professor Daniel Brooks examined traffic noise and found more frequent sleep disturbances among people living near major roads.Dr Sophia Chen investigated recycled materials in public buildings and reported that some could reduce construction costs.

Studied transport noise and sleep.3. Examined ways to reduce building expenses.4. Found a benefit of shaded streets during summer.

Complete using NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the text.E1. The drying stage lasts _____.E2. The seeds are stored in _____.

full.text: Reading passage

Paper is collected from offices and households. At the sorting centre, unsuitable material such as plastic is removed. The remaining paper is mixed with water to form pulp. Ink is then removed, and the cleaned pulp is pressed into sheets. Finally, the sheets are dried before packaging.
Full exercise A – Sentence Completion
Complete using NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage.1. Paper is collected from offices and _____.2. Paper and water form _____.3. Cleaned pulp is pressed into _____ before drying.

Complete using NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage.Paper is collected from offices and (1) _____. At a sorting centre, unsuitable materials such as (2) _____ are removed. The paper is mixed with water to produce (3) _____.

Complete the process using NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage.

rows: Sorting and removal of unsuitable material
